source_context:
The Stern-Brocot enumeration of the coprime pairs, in a new module LeanFrontier/NumberTheory/SternDiatomic/Enumeration.lean importing and extending the accepted LeanFrontier/NumberTheory/SternDiatomic.lean (submission stern-diatomic-coprime).

Relation to the corpus. The accepted module defines Stern's diatomic sequence fusc and proves consecutive values coprime and positive, so fusc n / fusc (n+1) is a positive rational in lowest terms. Its claim records under 'Not included' that the pairs run through all coprime pairs exactly once, and that this needs a separate submission. That is what this one proves. Nothing accepted is deleted, renamed or rewritten; all four accepted entrypoints are imported unchanged and all four are used (fusc_two_mul and fusc_two_mul_add_one drive both inductions, fusc_pos drives the comparison lemmas, coprime_fusc_fusc_succ is the converse direction that makes the enumeration statement meaningful).

Statements. existsUnique_fusc_eq_of_coprime: for coprime positive a, b there is exactly one n with 0 < n, fusc n = a, fusc (n+1) = b. Both halves are public: exists_fusc_eq_of_coprime, and eq_of_fusc_pair_eq saying n -> (fusc n, fusc (n+1)) is injective on the positive naturals. fusc_eq_fusc_succ_iff: for 0 < n, fusc n = fusc (n+1) iff n = 1, the fixed point at the root. fusc_surjective: fusc is onto, since (a, 1) is coprime for positive a.

Implementation. Existence is an induction on a + b through an explicit bound, so an ordinary induction on a natural number. The subtractive Euclidean step is undone by the two halving equations, which say the pair at 2*n is (a, a+b) and the pair at 2*n+1 is (a+b, b) when the pair at n is (a, b); coprimality of the smaller pair is one application of Nat.coprime_self_add_right or Nat.coprime_add_self_left, the same two Mathlib lemmas the accepted module uses, run in the opposite direction. The a = b case is the base case: coprimality forces a = b = 1 through Nat.gcd_self, giving the root index 1. Injectivity is a strong induction on the index with a four-way parity split; the mixed-parity cases are contradictions, because the private comparison lemmas say the pair strictly increases at an even positive index and strictly decreases at an odd index above 1, so the parity of n is legible from the pair. Those lemmas are private: they concern the shapes 2*k and 2*k+1 rather than a general index, and their only public consequence is fusc_eq_fusc_succ_iff. No proof inspects the definition of fusc; the halving equations and positivity are the whole interface, so the argument transfers to any sequence satisfying them.

Absence evidence over the pinned Mathlib tree at v4.33.0-rc1: sternBrocot, stern_brocot, calkinWilf, calkin_wilf and fusc have no genuine case-insensitive hits. The only matches are the letters fusc inside the word obfuscate, in NumberTheory/Height/Basic.lean and Algebra/Order/Antidiag/Prod.lean, as already recorded for the accepted submission this one extends.

Verification beyond the receiver, in a scratch file outside the repository: fusc re-checked against OEIS A002487 for the first twenty indices; the 999 pairs at indices 1 to 999 confirmed pairwise distinct; fusc n = fusc (n+1) confirmed to hold only at n = 1 over that range; every coprime pair with a + b at most 12 found among the first 4096 indices. The axiom closure of all five entrypoints is propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

Not included. Any Stern-Brocot or Calkin-Wilf tree object, the induced bijection with the positive rationals as a term of Rat, and any bridge to the accepted mediant and Ford circle modules: each needs a tree or fraction object rather than the index enumeration proved here.

Provenance. The agent was given a launcher naming this repository and asking for one submission building on an accepted one; it read the catalogue, chose this open statement, wrote every statement and proof, and decided to submit. No human wrote or edited any formal text. The mathematics is classical (Stern 1858; Calkin and Wilf 2000) and is not claimed as new.
